report:
Reviewed the full crates.sage_ir.types.body.closures claim and every current implementation/test association from a fresh review start. The claim has three linked requirements for a completed closure: a typed nested body, explicit parameters, and explicit captures. Captured the current closure checker branch, closure representation and parameter fields, the typed-IR completed-body context, and the accepted architectural-foundations completed-tree rationale.

The sole implementation association is the explicit TODO in sage_meta::todo in crates/sage-meta/tests/representation_spec.rs, explaining that closures and capture elaboration remain pending. The sole associated test, sage_meta::todo::types_body_closures, contains the same explanation and no assertions. There are no ordinary tests or implementation entries claiming this complete contract, and no N/A exemption. An execution of this empty test cannot establish closure behavior.

Current check/expr.rs retains a partial source-shaped path: it opens a lexical scope, checks parameter patterns into TyClosureParam entries, checks a nested expression body, allocates the parameter slice, and introduces a fresh type variable for TyExprData::Closure. The current Closure variant stores a parameter slice and nested expression pointer. TyClosureParam stores pattern, type, and source span. These support partial parameter/body representation, but the inspected representation has no explicit capture payload, and this branch is not evidence of a completed, fully resolved closure type. Thus the pending closure/capture elaboration prerequisite is concrete, rather than an unexplained placeholder. These dependencies are captured for assessing the deferral, not promoted to an ordinary implementation-completeness claim.

To replace the TODO, completed-closure elaboration must provide the typed nested body, explicit parameter representation and explicit captures, with associated tests directly inspecting those results. Useful distinguishing cases include no captures, references to enclosing locals, parameters shadowing enclosing names, and nested closures, so lexical scope handling cannot stand in for capture evidence. The destination remains a typed tree; the rationale does not require generator or other MIR lowering. All three claim requirements remain deferred as a complete guarantee, despite the existing partial body/parameter representation. No specification weakening is needed.

Validation was source inspection through review start/read. One attempted line read exceeded the short representation file and was retried successfully with valid bounds; it was not a behavioral failure. No behavioral tests or source edits were performed. Centrally executed suites are separate evidence and are not claimed as reviewer execution. No requested edits: the existing explicit implementation/test deferral honestly describes the unfinished closure and capture work.
